argument.notes: For n≥1 the finite grid has cost at most C n^(s/2)h^(s-n); for fixed δ>0 admissible h can tend to zero, giving zero content at every scale and hence zero measure. The extended-order conclusion D≤n follows from D≤s for all s>n without presupposing finite D. For n=0 the singleton has zero positive-exponent cost. The last finite ball cover proves finite content for arbitrary s,δ>0. Both clauses of N002 follow.

statement_closure.notes: n is a nonnegative integer, E⊆Eucl(n), and D is the extended nonnegative dimH(E). D001–D005 and D008 fix the metric, diameter, positive-exponent costs, measure and dimension. background_notes.fact: For compact K⊆Eucl(n), some L>0 satisfies K⊆[-L,L]^n. Open balls in the specified metric are open, and the positive-integer-radius balls centered at the origin cover Eucl(n).

grounds.reason: E is compact in the specified Euclidean metric.
Each point is a finite tuple with finite Euclidean distance to the origin.

background_notes.justification: The Archimedean property puts every finite point norm below a positive integer. Balls are open by the triangle inequality. Compactness supplies a finite subcover of these balls; choosing a positive integer at least every selected radius bounds the norm of each point of E. Each absolute coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean norm since its square is a summand in the norm square. This proves the displayed F001 witness existence, also in dimension zero.

background_notes.fact: For L>0, n≥1 and 0<h≤1, the interval [-L,L] admits a partition into m=ceil(2L/h) closed subintervals of length at most h. Their n-fold products cover [-L,L]^n, number at most (2L/h+1)^n≤(2L+2)^n h^(-n), and have diameter at most sqrt(n)h.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies a positive L whose coordinate box contains E.
The witness L is chosen, n≥1 is the open branch condition, and 0<h≤1 is imposed.
Distances are the square root of the sum of squared coordinate differences.

background_notes.justification: Here m≥1 and m≥2L/h, so equal subdivision gives length 2L/m≤h. Also m≤2L/h+1. Taking Cartesian products gives m^n sets; coordinate differences bounded by h give squared distance at most nh². Multiplying the count inequality by h^n reduces the final estimate to (2L+h)^n≤(2L+2)^n. Thus this verifies the finite grid construction already used in S002.

background_notes.fact: For finite K>0 and real p>0, Kh^p tends to zero as h decreases to zero, even under any additional fixed positive upper bound on h. Consequently nonnegative H^s_δ(E) bounded above by such admissible-cover costs is zero; if this holds for every δ>0, H^s(E)=0.

grounds.reason: n≥1, s>n, C=(2L+2)^n>0 and the grid gives cost ≤K h^p with K=C n^(s/2), p=s-n>0. The additional bounds are h≤1 and h≤δ/sqrt(n), both positive.
The content is an infimum of nonnegative cover costs, and the measure is the supremum of those contents over positive scales.

background_notes.justification: For ε>0, choose 0<h<min(1,δ/sqrt(n),(ε/K)^(1/p)). The ordinary monotonicity and inverse identities of positive real powers give Kh^p<ε. Hence each fixed-scale content is at most every positive ε and is zero by nonnegativity. Its supremum over scales is then zero. No limit interchange or measure continuity theorem is required.

background_notes.fact: For x∈[0,∞] and finite real b≥0, if x≤s for every real s>b then x≤b. This applies with x=D, b=n in S002 and with b=0 in S003.

grounds.reason: D initially lies in the extended nonnegative reals.
N001 is used after the cover estimate to obtain D≤s for each real s>n.
The zero-dimensional branch obtains D≤s for each positive real s and D≥0.

background_notes.justification: First x≤b+1 excludes infinity. If the resulting finite x were greater than b, the real midpoint s=(b+x)/2 would satisfy b<s<x, contradicting x≤s. For b=0, nonnegativity then yields x=0. The argument does not use real arithmetic on D before proving it finite.

background_notes.fact: For compact E in a metric space and real δ>0, the balls B(x,δ/4), x∈E, have a finite subcover of E, each with diameter at most δ/2. For any real s>0 this cover has finite total s-cost and is δ-admissible.

grounds.reason: s and δ are arbitrary positive reals and this family is explicitly chosen.
The ambient space carries the Euclidean metric.
Finite covers are admissible countable covers and give upper bounds on H^s_δ(E).

background_notes.justification: Every center belongs to its positive-radius open ball, so these open balls cover E and compactness gives finitely many. For points y,z in a chosen ball, the triangle inequality gives dist(y,z)<δ/2; taking the diameter supremum gives diam≤δ/2. A nonnegative finite diameter raised to a positive real power is finite, so the finite sum is finite and bounds the infimum defining content. In Eucl(0) every such nonempty ball is a singleton of diameter zero.
